history.period: Construction begun 1903 (completed c. 1912 per some accounts)
history.summary: THIS IS A JAIN TEMPLE, NOT A HINDU TEMPLE — keep-or-drop decision needed. Built by Sir Seth Hukumchand Jain, a prominent Jain trader and industrial pioneer, adjacent to his Shish Mahal mansion at Itwaria Bazar (now Sir Hukumchand Marg). The interior - floors, walls, columns and ceilings - is entirely covered with glass panels, mosaics and mirrors; craftsmen were brought from Jaipur and even Iran, and the ornamentation follows old/medieval Jain style with the innovation of multicoloured glass. It is the central institution of the Digambar Jain community of Indore; processions start or terminate here and collective kshamavani is organised here. Photography of the interior is generally prohibited. Coordinates here are from geocoding of the temple's address; Wikipedia lists 22.747, 79.869 (verify).

name: Kanch Mandir
town_description: Indore, the largest city and commercial capital of Madhya Pradesh, is a historic former seat of the Holkar dynasty and one of India's cleanest and most food-famous cities. Its old city around Rajwada and Itwaria Bazar holds some of the city's oldest religious and commercial landmarks, including this glass Jain temple.
